newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Good signs Australia growth will pick up - Fahey.
newsitem.headline: Good signs Australia growth will pick up - Fahey.

text.p: Australian Finance Minister John Fahey said on Sunday the domestic economy was healthy, despite some recent weak economic data, and that there were good signs for a pick up in economic growth.
Fahey said in a television interview there were signs of improving business confidence and a pick up in housing activity.
"There are some very good signs there and I'm sure growth will come with time," he told the Seven Network's Face to Face programme.
"Government creates the foundation, I believe we've done that and it will mean there is an opportunity for an increase in that activity which is pretty important to the jobs we need," he said.
The government forecast growth of 3.75 percent in the year to June 30, 1998 but there have been calls in the business community for the government to aim for growth of four percent or more.
March quarter gross domestic product (GDP) data due next Wednesday are expected to show annual growth falling to about 2.2 percent from 3.1 percent in the December quarter.

Asked about the chances of another interest rate cut to lift growth, Fahey said he did not comment on the future direction of rates, but added that low inflation meant the central bank could consider a rate cut if it saw the need to do so.

"I think what is there, though, is a recognition that with low inflation, most important, there is an opportunity for the Reserve Bank to look at it and to ensure that if there is a need to do it, they've at least got the basis to do it," he said.
Figures released on Friday showed retail sales dropped 1.7 percent in April, when average market forecasts were for a 0.5 percent rise.
Fahey said the government's 1997/98 budget announced earlier this month had locked in low inflation.
"There is sustainable growth there and some healthy signs that as each month goes on we'll see a pickup," he said.
"We're putting in place the ingredients of low inflation, which assists ... low interest rates, sustainable growth ... that's very good for our future," he added.
"We're going to see that growth, it's going to come this year and next year."
Fahey also added his voice to the call for a wide-ranging review of Australia's tax system.

"Let's have an open debate and let's allow all options, all taxes - whatever - to be examined thoroughly by the Australian people, and let's try and get that outcome that ensures that we have increased employment," he said.
